 Mikey Moore debunks transfer myth as Rangers told answer to January loan pitch
 The Tottenham kid is currently playing in Germany with FC Koln on loan
 Add to preferred sources Comments Sport Mark Pirie Assistant Live Sports Editor 09:19, 20 Nov 2026 View 2 Images (Image: Ralf Treese/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock) 
 Winger Mikey Moore insists he is happy with his decision to move to the Bundesliga last summer - despite murmurs over a January return to Rangers.
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 While Tottenham battled relegation last term, teenager Moore has impressed on loan in the Scottish Premiership and emerged as a key man for Rangers in their bid to land the title.
 ‌ 
 However, his form north of the border didn't earn the 19-year-old a crack at the Premier League and instead he penned a year-long loan deal with FC Koln.
 The England youth cap has struggled to hold down a regular starting spot in Germany sparking rumours his loan deal could be cut short by Spurs - but the wide man insists he is happy with the decision made to have a crack at a top five league.
 He told the BBC: "Over the years you've seen so many young players come out here, and there are good examples of world-class players like Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho doing really well.
 "It's a really attractive place to play football, especially for a young attacker. It's a great platform to play, and that was sold to me by the people at the club and the manager.
 ‌ 
 "They've put real trust in me, and the amount of game time I've played so quickly in my Koln career has been nice. It's been good to have that trust from all the staff and people at the club.
 "I'm already happy with my decision. Now I can really kick on, make my own story and build my own path in German football. I had options to stay in England and maybe stay somewhere a little more comfortable.
 ‌ 
 "But the conversations came down to me picking a team, and I wanted to take myself a little bit out of my comfort zone to test myself in one of the top five leagues. When we were speaking, everyone said they thought it would be a really good experience for me to experience this type of football.
 "It's really intense, and there are some great teams in the league. For me, it was a no-brainer. I made the decision early that I wanted to come out here, and now I just need to push on."
 ‌ 
 View 2 Images Mikey Moore of Rangers applauds the fans
 Speaking to Record Sport earlier this month, Moore revealed that talks over a return to Glasgow cooled following the arrival of Derek McInnes.
 ‌ 
 Chairman Andrew Cavenagh has insisted that there won't be any new additions in the January window - while McInnes looked to close the door on exits for key men like Nico Raskin and Olwethu Makhayna.
 But speaking to Clyde 1 Superscoreboard, former Rangers man Gordon Dalziel pitched a potential return: "There is no doubt that he would be a good addition to the squad, he was very successful when he came up here.
 Article continues below He added: "I wouldn't get too caught up in Derek McInnes' answer [on transfers] - of course, if there is a massive bid they can't refuse every player has got their price. I think there is only two that would command decent money just now [Raskin and Makhayna] and I think he will look to add to his squad."
